cover.title: Coverage meeting
cover.open.cold.1: Good to finally meet. You want to see our deal flow? Fine, let’s get to know each other.
cover.open.cold.2: I’ve heard the Poiesis name. Getting onto our lists takes a little time, though.
cover.open.cold.3: A coffee is always welcome. Information… we’ll work up to that.
cover.open.cold.4: There are a lot of houses out there. Show me why we should call you first.
cover.open.warm.1: Back again. I’ve kept an eye on the sector you mentioned.
cover.open.warm.2: Your house comes up in our team meetings these days. In a good way.
cover.open.warm.3: Have a seat. I have a few things for you today.
cover.open.warm.4: I watched how you handled your last process. Clean.
cover.close.1: Come in, close the door. This stays in the room.
cover.close.2: You’re at the top of our list, so you hear this first.
cover.close.3: Every MD here knows your name. I won’t send you away empty-handed.
cover.close.4: Here’s this quarter’s sell-side list before anyone else sees it.
cover.line.market.expansion.1: Pipelines are full. Sellers think this is the time. Be ready to pay up.
cover.line.market.expansion.2: Sellers are lining up at these multiples. We have five mandates this quarter alone.
cover.line.market.expansion.3: Every auction draws ten-plus bidders. Hold back in round one and you won’t make the shortlist.
cover.line.market.slowdown.1: It is cooling. Sellers have not lowered their hopes yet, and a few deals have broken.
cover.line.market.slowdown.2: Sellers remember last year’s prices, buyers see this year’s. The gap is wide.
cover.line.market.slowdown.3: More processes are pulled in round two. A buyer who can close is worth a lot now.
cover.line.market.recession.1: Frankly, nobody wants to sell. Only the ones who have to. There will be distressed chances.
cover.line.market.recession.2: Half my week is lender meetings. Plenty of companies are close to a covenant breach.
cover.line.market.recession.3: Those who buy now laugh later. Just check the cash flow twice.
cover.line.market.recovery.1: I think the bottom is behind us. Everything that was held back will come out in the first half.
cover.line.market.recovery.2: Owners are taking calls again. Successions shelved for a year are back on the table.
cover.line.market.recovery.3: Buy now and you buy the recovery at trough prices. Your rivals are still hesitating.
cover.line.credit.tight.1: Lenders have gone picky. Spreads at {spread}% make high leverage hard.
cover.line.credit.tight.2: Banks are cutting new acquisition loans. At {spread}% you will need more equity.
cover.line.credit.tight.3: A few private credit funds are still lending. With spreads at {spread}%, expect to pay up.
cover.line.credit.easy.1: Acquisition finance is plentiful. Spreads around {spread}%; lenders are chasing deals.
cover.line.credit.easy.2: Lending terms are good. {spread}%. That is when rival houses bid hard.
cover.line.credit.easy.3: Banks are writing loose covenants at {spread}% spreads. Windows like this don’t last.
cover.line.sector.1: An owner in {sector} is talking to banks. I cannot give you the name yet, but it will come out within {months} months.
cover.line.sector.2: Lots of succession talk among {sector} owners. One of them will be on the market in about {months} months.
cover.line.sector.3: A carve-out is being prepared in {sector}. The parent wants it done within {months} months.
cover.line.sector.4: A family company in {sector} gave up on the next generation. It should reach us in about {months} months.
cover.line.rival.1: {house} keeps looking at {sector}. Expect them in nearly every sale there.
cover.line.rival.2: Word is {house} wants a platform in {sector}. They’ll bid hard.
cover.line.rival.3: {house} came second on a {sector} deal last month. They’ll want to win the next one.
cover.line.pipeline.1: Between us: we have the mandate for {company}. The teaser goes out within {months} months. Take a look first.
cover.line.pipeline.2: We have {company}. The teaser goes out in {months} months. Meet the owner before then.
cover.line.pipeline.3: Keep this quiet until it’s public: {company} goes to market within {months} months.
cover.line.reputation.good.1: Your house has a good name on the street right now. Sellers know who you are.
cover.line.reputation.good.2: Sellers all heard you held your price to the end last time.
cover.line.reputation.good.3: Owners ask about your house by name now. It makes our introductions easy.
cover.line.reputation.bad.1: Your house's name is not great right now. Sellers worry whether you close.
cover.line.reputation.bad.2: Sellers remember the price you cut in the binding round. Tread carefully for a while.
cover.line.reputation.bad.3: Frankly, a couple of our MDs wanted you off the list. I talked them out of it.
